metadata.case_name: CHUM HOK CHING AND ANOTHER v. CHUNG LAI CHING

plaintiff.occupation_before: auto technician under a sole proprietorship

injuries.description: abrasion over the front of both knees; clinical diagnosis was knee contusion
source: According to the Medical Report dated 7 June 2010 of the Department of Accident & Emergency of QEH, the 1st plaintiff was examined by Dr Yip Sai Hang on 26 March 2010 at 23:16 hours, and he was found to have abrasion over the front of both knees, but x-ray showed no fracture. The clinical diagnosis was knee contusion.

injuries.description: soft tissue edema as well as large suprapatellar effusion; bone bruises in the posterior medial and lateral tibial plateaus; tear in the posterior horn of medial meniscus and intrasubstance tear lateral meniscus; ACL tear; partial tears medial and lateral collateral ligaments (right knee) - pre-existing injury
source: In the MRI scan report of the 1st plaintiff’s right knee by Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital dated 27 October 2009, the 1st plaintiff was found to have (1) soft tissue edema as well as large suprapatellar effusion, (2) bone bruises in the posterior medial and lateral tibial plateaus, (3) tear in the posterior horn of medial meniscus and intrasubstance tear lateral meniscus, (4) ACL tear, and (5) partial tears medial and lateral collateral ligaments.
injuries.icd_description: Injury to multiple structures of knee

injuries.description: post-concussion syndrome / mild traumatic brain injury
source: On 7 May 2012, the 2nd plaintiff consulted a specialist in neurosurgery, Dr Fung Ching Fai, and she was diagnosed with post-concussion syndrome.

injuries.description: a bald spot measured at 20 X 15mm, smooth flat and void of hair at the left posterior scalp
source: In the joint medical report dated 19 September 2011 by Dr Otto Au and Dr Ian Nicolson, both specialists in plastic surgery, both experts confirm that the 2nd plaintiff had (1) a bald spot measured at 20 X 15mm, smooth flat and void of hair at the left posterior scalp;
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of scalp

injuries.description: several abrasion scars over the dorsum and proximal wrist of the left hand, namely, a linear irregular scar at the radial surface of the proximal wrist measured 20 X 3mm, two round spots over the mid and ring fingers of the knuckle area measured 10 X 10mm and 7 X 7mm respectively; and scars on the right hand including a round scar measured 8 X 10mm over the wrist and a round scar over the knuckle area of the ring finger measured 10mm in diameter
source: In the joint medical report dated 19 September 2011 by Dr Otto Au and Dr Ian Nicolson, both specialists in plastic surgery, both experts confirm that the 2nd plaintiff had (2) several abrasion scars over the dorsum and proximal wrist of the left hand, namely, a linear irregular scar at the radial surface of the proximal wrist measured 20 X 3mm, but it was soft, smooth and barely visible, and two round spots over the mid and ring fingers of the knuckle area measured 10 X 10mm and 7 X 7mm respectively which is slightly raised and firm; and (3) at the right hand dorsum, a round scar measured 8 X 10mm over the wrist, which was soft, smooth and slightly visible, and a round scar over the knuckle area of the ring finger measured 10mm in diameter, which was soft and smooth.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple superficial injuries of wrist or hand

injuries.description: mild injury of the neck (soft tissue injury resulting in pain)
source: In the accident, there was also mild injury of the neck and low back. This would give rise to soft tissue injury resulting in pain, but there is no evidence for damage of the cervical spinal cord or root on clinical examination.
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain, stiffness or tenderness only

injuries.description: mild injury of the low back (soft tissue injury resulting in pain)
source: In the accident, there was also mild injury of the neck and low back. This would give rise to soft tissue injury resulting in pain, but there is no evidence for damage of the cervical spinal cord or root on clinical examination.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle, fascia or tendon of lower back

manifestations.description: Pain over both knees; pain aggravated by squatting for 5 to 10 minutes requiring relief by shifting weight or sitting
From surveillance video: shifting weight between legs while squatting and difficulty squatting for prolonged periods; walking with altered posture due to leg pain
Headache: continuous pain over the back of the left side of her head, throbbing, worse on exertion, often disturbs or prevents sleep
Dizziness: momentary bouts of light headedness about once a week causing brief loss of balance
Impaired cognition: less confident in ability to remember things, loses train of thought, impaired concentration and memory
Mood and personality changes: more easily irritated, gets depressed for no obvious reason (mild)
Loss of consciousness after the accident (brief coma/unconsciousness estimated about 10 minutes)
Bald spot at left posterior scalp (20 X 15mm) smooth, flat and void of hair
Multiple small scars over dorsum and proximal wrist of left hand and scars on right hand (measured sizes as in medical report)
Neck discomfort with limitation of rotation to the right; low back discomfort when twisting or bending

treatments_received: Accident & Emergency treatment at Queen Elizabeth Hospital (QEH)
General out-patient attendance at Anne Black Health Centre General Out-patient Clinic (ABHCGOPC)
Consultations with private consultants (Dr Au Wing Wah, Dr Clifford Loo, Dr Chau Yat Sang, Dr Or Chi Kong, Dr Fung Ching Fai, Dr Brian Choa, Dr Yu Yuk Ling)
Follow-up at Department of Neurosurgery of QEH and Occupational Therapy
Plastic surgery consultations and suggested excision revision for hand scars (assessed by plastic surgeons)
treatments_future: Plastic surgery (excision revision) for scars - surgeon's fee $10,000.00 and follow up charges $3,000.00
Course of a tricyclic drug such as Amitriptyline (estimated $15,000.00 over about 6 months) supervised by a neurologist or psychiatrist

losses.description: Reduced ability to squat, stand and perform prolonged repair work; pain after squatting for 5 to 10 minutes requiring relief (affecting ability to perform auto technician duties)
Bald spot at left posterior scalp and multiple scars on hands causing cosmetic disability and concern about appearance
Abrasion scars over dorsum and proximal wrist of the left hand and scars on the right hand (measured in joint medical report)
Mild mood and personality changes (more easily irritated, episodes of depression) attributed to post-concussion syndrome

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Gave up motorcycle rides and feels nervous in traffic after the accident
